question: What are the tech-enablement theses for every company?
html:
Tech-enablement theses by company

Each portfolio company gets a named operating system, built mostly from proven vendors plus a thin BSP data layer, to make earnings look more recurring and predictable to the next buyer (ServiceOS evidence, Oct 6, 2026). The evidence supports up to ~3 turns of quality premium. Tech can claim about 0.5–2.5 turns of it, and scale explains the 17–20x roll-up prints.

Company theses at a glance

CompanyOSCore thesisPremium (turns, est.)Agent value (est.)
Punctual ProsServiceOSBooking rate, pricebook, memberships1.0–2.5$0.9M
CETGridOSProject work into recurring O&M0.5–1.5$1.3M
FrontlineFirmOSSecurity and e-billing service lines0.5–1.5$3.6M
Thomas ScientificLabOSEBITDA and cost-to-serve, not multiple0.5–1.0$3.8M
BPISignalOSProductized monitoring0.5–2.0$2.3M
Fair HarborHarborOSFewer returns, less excess inventorynot shown$0.8M

Sources: (ServiceOS evidence; Portfolio AI-agent plan). Agent values are labelled analyst assumptions, not company data.

Evidence behind each thesis

  • Punctual Pros: HVAC call booking averages 38% versus 59% at 25+ technician shops. Pricebook adopters grew tickets 14% versus 8%. Most agents per revenue dollar go to missed calls, dispatch, options, memberships and permits (Portfolio AI-agent plan). The mature target is a mid-teens EBITDA margin (Public comparables).
  • CET: Turn solar and SCADA work into measured O&M. Add NuWave and EV monitoring revenue, with agents for bid selection and faster estimating. Buyers grew more selective as electrical M&A slowed to 99 deals in 2025.
  • Frontline: Build recurring security and e-billing revenue-cycle lines. The Aventis MSP curve runs from 5.2x to 11.2x. Entry was already ~12–15x (est.), which caps the upside.
  • Thomas Scientific: Leverage drives this exit, not the multiple. The benchmarks are Avantor's ~80% digital transactions and Grainger's ~15.6% digital growth versus ~2% rep-led growth. Support is weak for a multiple premium and medium for EBITDA.
  • BPI: Productize monitoring on Brandwatch and Zignal. Protect client confidentiality while drafting faster. The PPHC floor is ~8.4x versus a 10–13x estimated sponsor exit.
  • Fair Harbor: Use Shopify and Klaviyo to cut returns and excess inventory. The roadmap EBITDA range is $0.40–1.75M. The multiple-premium range for Fair Harbor was truncated in the dataset, so the full HarborOS record is needed before quoting one.

Caveats

  • The Champions (~18.5x) and Sila (~17x) multiples are press estimates.
  • Agent volumes are analyst estimates. They must be replaced with system-of-record counts.
  • The agent plan totals ~$12.7M (est.), not de-duplicated. Each company sits inside its roadmap range.

Next actions

  1. Pull system-of-record call, ticket, invoice and member counts to replace the assumed volumes, starting with the wave-one agents.
  2. Retrieve the full HarborOS multiple evidence for Fair Harbor.
  3. Baseline Punctual Pros booking rate and pricebook adoption against the 38% and 59% benchmarks.
  4. Pressure-test Frontline's premium case given its ~12–15x (est.) entry.

Each portfolio company gets a named operating system, built mostly from proven vendors plus a thin BSP data layer, to make earnings look more recurring and predictable to the next buyer (ServiceOS evidence, Oct 6, 2026). The evidence supports up to ~3 turns of quality premium. Tech can claim about 0.5–2.5 turns of it, and scale explains the 17–20x roll-up prints.

## Company theses at a glance

| Company | OS | Core thesis | Premium (turns, est.) | Agent value (est.) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Punctual Pros | ServiceOS | Booking rate, pricebook, memberships | 1.0–2.5 | $0.9M |

| Fair Harbor | HarborOS | Fewer returns, less excess inventory | not shown | $0.8M |

Sources: (ServiceOS evidence; Portfolio AI-agent plan). Agent values are labelled analyst assumptions, not company data.

## Evidence behind each thesis

- **Punctual Pros:** HVAC call booking averages 38% versus 59% at 25+ technician shops. Pricebook adopters grew tickets 14% versus 8%. Most agents per revenue dollar go to missed calls, dispatch, options, memberships and permits (Portfolio AI-agent plan). The mature target is a mid-teens EBITDA margin (Public comparables).

- **Frontline:** Build recurring security and e-billing revenue-cycle lines. The Aventis MSP curve runs from 5.2x to 11.2x. Entry was already ~12–15x (est.), which caps the upside.
- **Thomas Scientific:** Leverage drives this exit, not the multiple. The benchmarks are Avantor's ~80% digital transactions and Grainger's ~15.6% digital growth versus ~2% rep-led growth. Support is weak for a multiple premium and medium for EBITDA.
- **BPI:** Productize monitoring on Brandwatch and Zignal. Protect client confidentiality while drafting faster. The PPHC floor is ~8.4x versus a 10–13x estimated sponsor exit.

- The Champions (~18.5x) and Sila (~17x) multiples are press estimates.
- Agent volumes are analyst estimates. They must be replaced with system-of-record counts.
- The agent plan totals ~$12.7M (est.), not de-duplicated. Each company sits inside its roadmap range.
